novelty_basis: J. Kari, V. Salo, I. Torma, Surjective two-neighbor cellular automata on prime alphabets (2013) - surjective two-neighbour CA over prime alphabets are permutive in some coordinate (https://research.utu.fi/converis/portal/detail/Publication/3119276; notes https://villesalo.com/notes/STNCAoPANotes.html); G. A. Hedlund, Math. Systems Theory 3 (1969). Our exhaustive check is an independent confirmation for n = 2, 3; the order-4 band illustrates why primality is needed.
proof_check: computer-assisted - exact pair-graph (Garden-of-Eden) decision for all 16 tables of order 2 and all 1734 classes of order 3 (invariant under isomorphism and mirror image), Hedlund's theorem for permutive => surjective; the order-4 example by a two-line argument (identity x shift) and the same decision procedure (EXP-C15-05)
statement: For |M| <= 3 the automaton c'_i = c_i * c_{i+1} is surjective on bi-infinite rows iff all rows or all columns of the table are permutations (1, 6, 420 surjective tables of orders 1, 2, 3 = 2(n!)^n - Lat(n)); for |M| = 4 the rectangular band (b,c)*(b',c') = (b,c') is surjective and injective but not permutive.
title: Surjective iff permutive for magmas of order at most 3; false at order 4
